inventory.name: window rawgamepadinputchange event and gamepad input snapshot

errors.rationale: The page describes passive event dispatch and reading a gamepad snapshot, not an operation with a return, rejection, or exception path; its API-shape section names no errors.

securityPrivacy.rationale: This page documents no security or privacy dimension for the event; the closest rendered fragment, #at-a-glance, records trial requirements but no permission, data-exposure, or privacy contract. This is recorded coverage debt, not a claim that gamepad input has no security or privacy implications.

notes: B3 ids-only edit: five existing h2 headings gained ids for the mapped dimensions; existing citations were already linked and no new href was added. securityPrivacy is not-applicable ONLY as an honest record that the existing page does not document that dimension, not a conclusion that the feature itself lacks privacy implications; #at-a-glance is the nearest rendered requirements fragment. Source/page divergence, observed 2026-10-07, neither side adjudicated or rewritten: this page calls the event rawgamepadinputchange and claims event.timestamp (DOMHighResTimeStamp), while ChromeStatus's origin-trial stage description (https://chromestatus.com/api/v0/features/5989275208253440) and the current proposal (https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/GamepadEventDrivenInputAPI/explainer.md) call it gamepadrawinputchanged; the proposal lists event.gamepad, axesChanged, buttonsValueChanged, buttonsPressed, buttonsReleased, and touchesChanged, with timestamp on gamepad.timestamp, not event.timestamp. The linked W3C Gamepad specification https://w3c.github.io/gamepad contains Gamepad.timestamp and the existing polling API, but no rawgamepadinputchange event definition. The page says Chrome 149 origin trial; ChromeStatus's origin-trial stage does list desktop_first 149, but the live browser status says In development with no shipping milestone (its separate stage_type 130 lists 147, not the OT stage). The page says Blink>Input>Gamepad, whereas ChromeStatus lists Blink>GamepadAPI. The page says polling introduces up to 16 ms at 60 Hz; the proposal says average ~8.33 ms at 60 Hz, which is a different metric, not necessarily a contradiction. Independent primary-source review and a disclosure sentence remain pending.
